title: NovoSpaRc: flexible spatial reconstruction of single-cell gene expression with optimal transport

nodes.text: novoSpaRc is a computational framework that probabilistically assigns single cells to tissue locations by formulating spatial reconstruction as an optimal transport problem, outputting a transport matrix mapping cells to locations and inferred spatial gene expression.
nodes.evidence: novoSpaRc, a computational framework that probabilistically assigns cells to tissue locations ... We formulated this hypothesis within the framework of optimal transport(OT)

nodes.text: novoSpaRc rests on a structural correspondence hypothesis: cells in physical proximity share similar gene expression profiles, so expression changes continuously rather than abruptly across space for a substantial subset of genes.
nodes.evidence: a structural correspondence hypothesis, that cells in physical proximity share similar gene expression profiles

nodes.text: Unlike prior reconstruction methods that require a spatial reference atlas of marker genes, novoSpaRc can reconstruct gene expression de novo without any reference atlas, while optionally incorporating one to improve performance.
nodes.evidence: a new computational approach that can spatially reconstruct gene expression without the need of a reference atlas, while being able to incorporate it and enhance performance if such an atlas exists

nodes.text: novoSpaRc computes three cost matrices (cell-cell expression distance, location-location physical distance, and optional atlas cell-location distance), using shortest paths along kNN graphs to capture nonlinear low-dimensional manifold structure.
nodes.evidence: we construct k-nearest-neighbors (kNN) graphs (based on Euclidean distances) in physical space and in gene expression space. The corresponding cost matrices consist of pairwise distances ... computed as the shortest paths along the corresponding kNN graphs

nodes.text: An alpha parameter interpolates between pure de novo structural-correspondence reconstruction (alpha=0, a Gromov-Wasserstein-style objective) and reconstruction driven solely by the reference atlas (alpha=1).
nodes.evidence: The alpha parameter is used to interpolate between two modes of reconstruction: (1) a de novo spatial reconstruction (α = 0) ... and (2) a reconstruction based only on the information provided by the reference atlas ... (α = 1)

nodes.text: novoSpaRc addresses the loss of spatial information inherent to scRNA-seq, which requires tissue dissociation, by deciphering spatial structure from existing single-cell data.
nodes.evidence: Most scRNA-seq methods, however, require dissociation of the tissue, which results in the loss of spatial information

nodes.text: novoSpaRc maps a scRNA-seq dataset of 10,000 cells onto 1,000 locations in under 5 minutes.
nodes.evidence: NovoSpaRc maps a scRNA-seq dataset of 10,000 cells onto 1,000 locations in <5 min

nodes.text: novoSpaRc reconstructed the mouse organ of Corti de novo using only the structural correspondence assumption along a 1D apex-to-base target axis.
nodes.evidence: we reconstruct the mouse organ of Corti de novo based on the structural correspondence assumption

nodes.text: novoSpaRc reconstructed human osteosarcoma cultured cells using marker gene information, with cell locations deduced from MERFISH microscope imaging.
nodes.evidence: human osteosarcoma cultured cells based on marker gene information ... cell locations are deduced from microscope imaging obtained using multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH)

nodes.text: novoSpaRc supports flexible target spaces (1D/2D/3D basic shapes or experimentally-derived coordinates) that should resemble the tissue-of-origin's shape or symmetries for optimal reconstruction.
nodes.evidence: the shape of the target space should resemble the shape (or underlying symmetries) of the tissue-of-origin

nodes.text: novoSpaRc can incorporate prior knowledge via nonuniform marginal distributions reflecting cell density or technical read quality, rather than assuming uniform marginals by default.
nodes.evidence: where prior biological knowledge exists for the physical density of cells, or where there is varying technical quality of cells, this can be readily incorporated

nodes.text: High spatial correlation between reference-atlas gene expression and novoSpaRc's predicted expression serves as a cross-validation metric for tuning parameters such as alpha.
nodes.evidence: high spatial correlation between the expression of genes from the reference atlas and their predicted expression indicates successful reconstruction and, therefore, can be used to cross-validate
